title: Why Russell Westbrook is a better passer than Steph Curry
text:
NBA fans argue about everything, who’s the GOAT, who’s more clutch, who locks up on defense. But today, we’re looking at a different debate: who’s the better passer, Russell Westbrook or Stephen Curry? At first glance, it seems easy. Russ has the triple-doubles and crazy assist numbers. Steph is known for deep threes and off-ball movement. But raw assist stats don’t tell the whole story. To really figure it out, we’ll look at assists per game, assist-to-turnover ratio, and how scoring and passing go together. So let’s break it down. Russ vs. Steph: who’s the better passer?


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(hoopR)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggtext)

Players<- load_nba_player_box(2009:2024) |> filter(team_name!="All-Stars") |> 
filter(team_name !="Team LeBron") |> 
filter(team_name!="Team Giannis") |> 
filter(team_name!="Leb") |> 
filter(team_name!="Team Stephen")

Players <- Players |> 
  mutate(free_throw_assists = sample(0:5, n(), replace = TRUE))
seasontotals <- Players |> 
  group_by(athlete_display_name,season,team_name) |> 
  summarise(
    totalminutes=sum(minutes, na.rm=TRUE),
    totalpoints=sum(points, na.rm=TRUE),
    totalassists=sum(assists, na.rm =TRUE),
    totalturnovers=sum(turnovers, na.rm =TRUE),
    games_played = n(), 
    assist_per_game=sum(assists, na.rm = TRUE) / n()
  ) |>
  mutate(assist_to_turnover=totalassists/totalturnovers)
RW<-seasontotals |> filter(athlete_display_name=="Russell Westbrook")
SC<-seasontotals |> filter(athlete_display_name=="Stephen Curry")

ggplot() + 
  geom_line(
    data=RW,
    aes(x=season,y=assist_to_turnover),
    color="#007AC1"
    )+
    geom_line(
    data=SC,
    aes(x=season,y=assist_to_turnover),
    color="#FFC72C"
    )+


  labs(
    title = "Russ at his best is better than Curry, but at his worst...",
    x = "",
    y = "Assist-to-Turnover Ratio",
    color = "Player",
    subtitle="When looking at these two point guards Curry is as steady can be, while peak Russ is better bad Russ is way worse.", 
    caption="Source: HoopR | By: A.J. Morgan"
    ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 7), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=9), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    ) 









As you see from this chart when looking at Westbrook and Curry their styles couldn’t be more different. Westbrook is a high-energy, high-risk playmaker who thrives in transition and racks up assists,but also turns the ball over a lot. Curry is more controlled, using his gravity and smart reads to make safer, efficient passes, even if he doesn’t get as many assists. Assist-to-turnover ratio is a great stat to look at, however it doesn’t show the full picture. To really see how they’ve impacted the game as passers, we need to look at their assists over time. Who stayed consistent? Who peaked when it mattered? Let’s check out this step chart to find out.


Code
logs <- read_csv("https://hoopr.sportsdataverse.org/")
careerassists<-Players |> 
  group_by(athlete_display_name,season) |> 
  summarise(total_assists=sum(assists, na.rm=TRUE)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  group_by(athlete_display_name) |> 
  arrange(season) |> 
  mutate(Cumassists = cumsum(total_assists))
RWassists<-careerassists|> filter(athlete_display_name=="Russell Westbrook")
SCassists<-careerassists|> filter(athlete_display_name=="Stephen Curry")
ggplot() + 
  geom_step(data=careerassists, aes(x=season, y=Cumassists, group=athlete_display_name), color="lightgrey") +
  geom_step(data=RWassists, aes(x=season, y=Cumassists, group=athlete_display_name), color="#007AC1") +
  geom_step(data=SCassists, aes(x=season, y=Cumassists, group=athlete_display_name), color="#FFC72C") +
  geom_point(data=RWassists |> filter(season == max(season)), aes(x=season, y=Cumassists, group=athlete_display_name), color="#007AC1") +
  geom_point(data=SCassists|> filter(season == max(season)), aes(x=season, y=Cumassists, group=athlete_display_name), color="#FFC72C") +
  geom_text_repel(data=RWassists |> filter(season == max(season)), aes(x=season, y=Cumassists, group=athlete_display_name, label = athlete_display_name)) +
  geom_text_repel(data=SCassists|> filter(season == max(season)), aes(x=season, y=Cumassists, group=athlete_display_name, label = athlete_display_name))+ 
  labs(
    title = "Russ and Curry assists overtime shows Westbrooks consistancy",
    x = "Years",
    y = "Assist overtime",
    color = "Player",
    subtitle="Through the first half of their careers they're pretty close however after 2020 westbrook really seperates himself.", 
    caption="Source: HoopR | By: A.J. Morgan"
    ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 7), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=9), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    )









Westbrook has the most total assists over time against some of the toughest defenses in the league. While Curry’s assist numbers are solid and consistent, Russ’s volume and pace put him well ahead of not just Steph, but most guards across the NBA. However raw assist totals only show one side of the story. What happens when you factor in scoring too? This final chart looks at both total points and total assists, giving us a fuller picture of overall offensive impact.


Code
ggplot() + 
  geom_point(data=seasontotals, aes(x=totalpoints, y=totalassists), color="lightgrey")+
  geom_point(data=RW, aes(x=totalpoints, y=totalassists), color="#007AC1")+
  geom_point(data=SC, aes(x=totalpoints, y=totalassists), color="#FFC72C")+ 
  labs(
    title = "Russ vs Curry Scoring and Passing",
    x = "Total Points",
    y = "Total Assists",
    color = "Player",
    subtitle = "When looking at scoring and passing <span style = 'color:#007AC1;'>Russell</span> stays ahead of<span style = 'color:#FFC72C;'> Curry</span> when it comes to scoring and passing.", 
    caption="Source: HoopR | By: A.J. Morgan"
    ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_textbox_simple(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    )









And once again, Westbrook stands out, not just as a passer, but as a dual threat who racks up numbers in both areas at a level few others can match. So, who’s the better passer? The numbers don’t lie. Curry might be the more efficient playmaker, however Westbrook’s total impact as a passer ,from volume, to consistency, to how he pairs it with his scoring, gives him the edge. After this Where does Curry stand? Still one of the smartest and most creative guards in the league, but in this debate, the edge goes to Russell Westbrook.
